title: Feedback That Changes What Happens Next

audience.who: corporate employees who give feedback to peers or direct reports
audience.knows: feedback matters, has given or received the vague kind and watched nothing change
audience.cares_about: getting a colleague to actually do something different without damaging the working relationship

outcome: After watching, the viewer can take one real piece of feedback they have been putting off and reshape it into a specific observed behaviour, its effect, and a clear request for what to do next time, ready to say this week.
through_line: Feedback fails when it describes how you feel about a person, and works when it hands them something they can see, picture and do differently.

arc_plan.what: Open on a colleague, a manager who tells a teammate after a tense meeting that they need to be more professional. The teammate nods warmly, and the same thing happens at the next meeting. This is the running example.
Tell the viewer they will leave able to rebuild that same sentence so it lands as something the colleague can act on, and that the kind tone was never the problem.
Show why the first attempt felt kind yet changed nothing: it was about the person's character and the speaker's feelings, so the listener had nothing to repeat or stop.
Part one, replace the label with what was observed: the specific moment, said as what anyone watching would have seen, not a judgement about the person.
Part two, add the effect: what that moment did to the team or the work, so the behaviour matters to the listener beyond the speaker's opinion.
Part three, end with a concrete request for next time and a way to check back, so the listener leaves with an action rather than a mood.
Give the viewer two or three versions of feedback aimed at the same colleague and have them pick which one names a behaviour, an effect and a request, and say why the others fail.
Invite the viewer to pick one real conversation they have been avoiding and draft its opening line in the same shape, using the running example as the pattern to follow.
Return to the opening meeting. The manager says the rebuilt sentence, the colleague has something specific to do, and the next meeting visibly goes differently.

must_cover.what: Vague, character-based feedback leaves the listener with feelings but nothing to change
Describe specific observable behaviour, not personality or intent
Name the effect the behaviour had on others or on the work
Make a clear request for what to do next time, and agree how to follow up
A check where the viewer tells effective feedback from vague feedback on the same situation

must_avoid: Statistics or research claims without a source in the approved knowledge sheet
Invented sayings presented as real or attributed to named experts
Opening with a textbook explanation of what feedback is, or an agenda of what the video will cover
Lecturing tone or childish framing; the viewer is a capable colleague
Separate unrelated examples that each appear once instead of the running example
Presenting one named feedback model as the only valid one
example_posture: One running example, a manager and a teammate after a tense meeting, carries the whole lesson. Show the weak sentence, then rebuild it one part at a time, and use the same colleague in the check and the payoff. Keep it ordinary workplace, believable, no villains.
visual_direction: Cartoon workplace story with the same two characters throughout. Show a sentence on a board that is visibly rebuilt piece by piece, a before and after of the same meeting, and a moment where a vague remark fades while a specific one stays. One loud thing on screen at a time; the rule is large when it is named.
voice_note: Mentor: warm, direct and a little dry, like a trusted senior colleague who has made this mistake too. Name each idea only after the viewer has seen it happen.
open_questions: Should the build name an established feedback model, or teach the three parts in plain words only? Left to the approved knowledge sheet.
Is there a specific workplace setting or industry the requester wants for the running example? None given, so a generic office is assumed.
